statement: The print file meets the fdm-print pack's support-free rules for a 0.4 mm printer, belly-down
rationale: Requirement R3. This claim has no number of its own: the fdm-print pack's seven evaluators each judge against a limit the model publishes, with its reason beside it in model/pigeon.py: overhang past 45 degrees on at most 0.5 % of the surface, flat bridges of at most 5 mm, cantilevers of at most 2 mm, the part inside a 180 mm bed less the brim (the bed is assumption C32), a thinnest section of at least three lines, the one slender member loaded along its layers, and under 24 h and one spool by a rough estimate. They read face angles and flat ceilings off the print file (input fdm-whistle-printing-notes, section 7, records what they do). They do not slice. They cannot see a layer that starts in mid-air (C12), a leak (C13) or a windway that closes up (C16), and they cannot tell a reachable overhang from a trapped one. That it prints is C24.

mechanism.how: The fdm-print pack: the model's published numbers against the process limits, and the print file's faces against the overhang and bridge limits, in the pose the file is in (belly down).
